analysis.title: Interest Rates Daily: Playing catch-up
key_insights: The BoE raised Bank Rate by 25bp to 4% on 5 Nov. The vote to hike was unanimous, with Catherine Mann dissenting in favour of 50bp. The tone was hawkish but the BoE did not precommit to a path and kept a clear focus on the Middle East.
The BoE's updated inflation projections show a peak of 4.9% in Q2 2027 and a 1Y-ahead forecast around 4%, which is coherent with at least one more hike.
Dec 2027 MPC-matched OIS rose 7bp and now prices 13bp of implied hikes. The 1YF1Y SONIA OIS is unchanged at 4.72%.
CA-CIB thinks a December BoE hike would need a renewed spike in energy prices. February is seen as the more likely next hike, alongside the MPR and the annual Agent's pay survey.
The BoE was late to tightening, but there is no meaningful payback because oil and gas futures fell sharply on hopes for a resolution of the Middle East conflict.
G10 curve dynamics are converging. The co-movement with energy prices is concentrated at the very front end, while segments beyond June 2027 remain decoupled from energy.
The 6M+ horizon is trading the sustainability of higher rate levels, which is a trade-off between inflation, monetary policy passthrough and growth.
Further progress toward ending the conflict could fuel policy divergence because central bank reaction functions differ.
For energy importers like the Eurozone, nine months of high energy prices feeding into wages is weighed against the activity drag and tighter financial conditions from rate hikes.

In the US, as long as the labour market is not a major source of inflationary pressure, the driver beyond the terminal rate is whether the expansion can continue despite lower fiscal impulse and a potential AI capex slowdown. Today's NFP is a first test.

tension_points.bull_case: Hawkish BoE tone, a 4.9% inflation peak in Q2 2027 and MPC members open to further hikes support another increase.
tension_points.bear_case: The BoE did not precommit, future hikes are conditional on labour market and second-round effects, and falling oil and gas prices on hopes of a conflict resolution reduce the pressure.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A renewed spike in energy prices would bring a December hike. Without it, February is the more likely next hike.
